vulnerabilityAlerts.description: The one class of update that stays manual. These bypass the release-age cooldown by design (that is the point of a security alert), and a hijacked package typically ships its payload AS a version that resolves an advisory -- so automerging here would hand same-day, unreviewed CI execution to precisely the most attacker-timed PRs, and this repo's CI holds real secrets (GEMINI_TOKEN, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, AI_LOCAL_TOKEN). The site is static, so a delayed fix carries almost no runtime risk, while a bad automerge carries a real one. They land immediately and are labelled, so they are visible at a glance; merging is a deliberate click.

packageRules.description: Every non-major update, all managers, lands in one PR that merges itself once the CI Gate passes. Nothing here should need a human on a normal month. This also automerges github-actions and pip_requirements, which used to be manual; Python bumps are covered by the Python Script Tests job, but note that job runs pytest and ruff only -- it does not exercise the GitHub/ORCID/AI network paths, which still surface first on the monthly run.

Majors automerge too, all in one PR of their own: the repo is rarely tended, so a month's updates should arrive as two PRs, not one per major. Kept apart from the non-major group so a major that breaks the build holds back only the other majors, never the routine updates. One group also keeps majors that must move in lockstep (astro with @astrojs/*, react with @types/react) together without per-monorepo rules. The 14-day age is the real safety mechanism: it means this repo is never the first to hit a broken release. Safe only because CI Gate (typecheck, build, unit, e2e, visual regression, Python scripts) is the required status check on main -- automerge waits on required checks only, so if CI Gate is ever dropped from branch protection this silently becomes merge-without-testing. Note the Cloudflare preview job is deliberately NOT required: preview.yml has a paths filter that skips .github/**, and a workflow skipped by a paths filter never reports a status, so requiring it would deadlock every actions-only PR forever. Actions that only the preview, deploy or monthly workflows exercise (wrangler-action, sticky-pull-request-comment, create-github-app-token, create-pull-request, upload-artifact) merge with their group too: a break there cannot take the live site down -- a failed deploy never replaces the live Pages deployment and the smoke check opens an issue -- it only surfaces as a failed preview step or a failed monthly run.

TypeScript 7 is the native (Go) compiler and does not yet ship the programmatic API that `astro check` -- the Typecheck step of the CI Gate -- relies on; the check aborts with 'does not expose the programmatic API'. Hold TypeScript below 7 so it cannot block the majors group, and delete this rule once @astrojs/language-server supports TypeScript 7.
